passage: In the school computer lab, Eshaan had a tab open with Riya's holiday photos, then Kabir's football clips, then Jasmine's party. Everyone seemed to be laughing. He scrolled until the bell rang, feeling small. Mridul sir, the lab teacher, glanced at the screen as he shut down the computers. "Nice trip," he said mildly. "Whose?" "Just someone's," Eshaan muttered. Later he thought about Riya's post from last week, the one saying she couldn't sleep before exams. It had been buried under all the smiling pictures. He wasn't sure why the thought helped. He deleted the tabs, and signed up for the coding club that had been posted outside the lab for a month, even though it felt awkward.

qa.q: Who glanced at Eshaan's screen in the computer lab?
How was Eshaan feeling as he scrolled through the photos, and what changed his mind?
qa.a: He felt small and envious. Remembering Riya's post about not sleeping before exams showed him the smiling pictures hid worries too.

qa.q: What could Eshaan do with his envy?
qa.a: Notice that online pictures are curated, avoid tearing anyone down and build his own strengths, as he began by joining the coding club.

qa.q: How might Mridul sir see what Eshaan was doing?
qa.a: Probably as a student feeling left out. He mildly asked whose trip it was rather than scolding, which leaves space for Eshaan to talk if he chooses.

grounding: The protagonist envies popular classmates online, notices that curated images hide worries and turns to building his own strengths.

passage:
Every night Binita scrolled through Madhuri's photos. Madhuri at the beach. Madhuri with her perfect friends. Madhuri winning the debate trophy, hair perfect, smile perfect. Binita would put the phone down feeling small and ugly.
She even started a comment once, something mean about Madhuri's dress. She deleted it, but thought about it for hours.
Then on Thursday, in the girls' washroom, she found Madhuri crying by the sink.
"Are you okay?"
Madhuri wiped her face. "My parents fight every night. And if I don't top, my dad goes silent for a week. Don't tell anyone."
Binita walked back to class stunned. None of that was in the photos.
That night, instead of scrolling, she opened her sketchbook, the one she'd abandoned in Class 8. She drew for an hour. It wasn't perfect. It was hers.
The next day she smiled at Madhuri in the corridor. Madhuri smiled back, a real one.

qa.q: Where did Binita find Madhuri crying?
qa.a: By the sink in the girls' washroom.

qa.q: How did Binita feel after scrolling Madhuri's photos?
qa.a: She felt small, ugly and envious, even tempted to write something mean.

qa.q: What did Binita realise, and how did she respond?
qa.a: She saw that the perfect photos hid real worries, so she put down the phone and returned to her own sketching.

qa.q: What might it be like for Madhuri behind her perfect photos?
qa.a: Madhuri feels stressed and sad, dealing with parents who fight and pressure to top that nobody sees online.

grounding: A teen who envies a popular classmate's online life learns the images hide worries and turns to building her own strengths.

passage:
"Zeenat, look at Tamanna's new post. Another trip. Another perfect selfie."
"Sabina, you've shown me four of her posts today."
"Because her life is ridiculous. Everyone loves her. She has everything."
"You don't even know her."
"I know enough. I'm writing, 'Filter much?' under this one."
"Please don't."
"Why not? It's true."
"Because last month her brother was in hospital for two weeks. She didn't post a single thing about that. You only see the good bits."
"…Oh. I didn't know."
"Nobody knows. That's the point."
Sabina put the phone down. "I just feel so boring next to her."
"You're the best singer in our year. When did you last practise?"
"Months ago."
"Then maybe spend tonight on that instead of on her page."
Sabina deleted the comment. Later that night, she sent Zeenat a voice note of herself singing, slightly off-key, but hers.

qa.q: How many of Tamanna's posts had Sabina shown Zeenat that day?
What was Sabina feeling while scrolling Tamanna's posts?
qa.a: She felt envious and boring by comparison, enough to want to write a mean comment.

qa.q: What helped Sabina change direction, and why?
qa.a: Zeenat reminded her that posts hide worries and pointed her back to her own singing, so she built her strengths instead of tearing Tamanna down.

qa.q: How might Tamanna feel if she saw 'Filter much?' under her post?
qa.a: She might feel hurt and attacked, especially after a hard month with her brother in hospital that nobody knew about.

grounding: A teen who envies a popular classmate's online life learns that posts hide worries and focuses on her own strengths instead of tearing her down.
